transport: None of its own — a passive 47 kΩ NTC thermistor on a 2-pin 3.81 mm plug into the controller's temperature port (❽ "RTS interface" on Tracer-AN 50-100A, ① on XTRA-N). 3 m standard cable, customizable; vendor caps the sampling run at 20 m. No address, no baud, no framing — the reading reaches the hub only through the host charge controller's own Modbus map.
refutedOnReview: REFUTED — and not on a technicality. The cited sources are real and do name the model, but none of them documents a register map, and the device cannot have one. gotchas: Not a device. It is a two-wire NTC thermistor with no protocol at all — nothing to poll, address, or discover, and no driver to write. It does not create a device record; it changes what an existing solar-charger reports. If the catalogue files it as an environment-sensor it will imply a driver that cannot exist. It be

The reading surfaces only through the host controller's existing map: input register 0x3110 in epever-tracer-a, already mapped to battery-temperature in crates/drivers/cabin-epever/src/xtra.rs. Nothing to add to the driver for this part; fitting it is a wiring change, not a code change.

Battery over-heat protection stops at >65 °C and resumes below 55 °C. Lithium Low Temperature Protection Threshold defau
unmappedReports: Probe fitted / probe fault. The manuals define a real degraded state — probe missing, short-circuited or damaged → silent fallback to an assumed 25 °C with compensation off — and there is no MetricKind or fault signal that can express it. The system cannot tell a measured 25 °C from an assumed one, so the degradation is invisible exactly when it matters., No MetricKind distinguishes a battery temperature sensed at the bank from one sensed at the controller's own local probe. Both land on battery-temperature, and that distinction is the entire reason this part is sold. A variant, or a per-reading provenance flag, would let the hub say which one it is holding., Temperature compensation coefficient (-3 mV/°C/2V default, forced to 0 for lithium) and the lithium Low Temperature Protection Threshold (0 °C default, range 10 ~ -40 °C) are controller settings this probe drives. Neither has a MetricKind to read it back nor a CommandKind to set it — so the hub cannot report or change how the charger is acting on the temperature it is being handed.
